authority: Cambridge International AS & A Level Computer Science 9618 syllabus, 2027-2029, Version 2

records.resolution: Adds visible CORE teaching, practice and two assessment forms for the basic Von Neumann architecture and shared-memory stored-program concept.
Distinguishes general- and special-purpose registers and teaches PC, MDR, MAR, ACC, IX, CIR and status roles without losing the Cambridge ACC question convention.
Teaches ALU, CU, system clock and Immediate Access Store roles and the boundary that IAS is memory rather than a register or cache.
Explains address, data and control bus purposes, directions and coordinated memory-read use.
Covers processor type, cores, bus width, clock and cache as workload-dependent factors rather than isolated guarantees.
Adds accurate USB, HDMI and VGA signal/use distinctions and direct assessment.
Preserves the fetch-execute sequence with register-transfer notation and distinct MDR-to-CIR transfer and PC update.
Adds interrupt causes/applications, cycle-boundary detection, priority, state save, ISR, restore and correct resumption.
Relates processor-specific assembly mnemonics and operands to assembler-produced binary machine instructions.
Teaches and assesses pass 1 address/symbol-table work and pass 2 translation with resolved symbols.
Provides an executable-instruction trace method and indexed-address trace assessment with register and memory effects.
Groups every specified opcode under data movement, input/output, arithmetic, branch or compare according to official effects.
Uses the full Version 2 instruction set and rejects the former LDR-relative, CMI-immediate, JPE-equal and JPN-negative semantics.
Teaches immediate, direct, indirect, indexed and relative addressing and replaces the four-mode visual with a complete five-mode diagram.
Keeps masks and all logical, arithmetic and cyclic left/right shifts in visible CORE content, verifies every example at eight-bit fixed width and leaves pipelining OPTIONAL.
